title: The 90-Second Morning Check That Keeps You Out of Spam
description: Three numbers to check every morning to protect your cold email inboxes, plus the Claude prompt that checks every inbox for you.
lead: This is the 90-second morning check from the reel, plus the Claude prompt that does it for you. Three numbers, every morning, before your emails go out.
insider: We run this check every day on every client inbox. It's why our 5-day blitz sent **96,408 emails with a 0.45% bounce rate**. The check takes 90 seconds. Knowing what to do when a number goes red, and doing it the same day, is what keeps a campaign alive, and that's our job for clients.

head: Check
Green
If it's red
rows: Pause the campaign and clean the list
Lower that inbox's daily limit, keep warm-up on
Stop that inbox and check its DNS records

blocks.text: Instantly's own guide says to keep bounces under 2%, and its minimum health score is 90%. Aim higher, at 95, so you have a safety margin.

blocks.label: Claude Code prompt
blocks.text:
Check my cold email setup in Instantly. For every inbox, give me: bounce rate for the last 7 days, warm-up health score, and daily sending limit.
Flag in red: any inbox with bounces over 2%, health under 95, or no warm-up.
For each red inbox, tell me the one action to take today (pause it, lower its limit, or check DNS). Keep the healthy inboxes sending.
Show the result as a table, worst inboxes first.
Pause only the bad inbox. Keep the rest sending, so one problem doesn't stop the whole campaign.
It only works if you act the same day a number goes red.

faq.q: How do I run a spam test?
faq.a: Send an email from the inbox to a few test accounts (Gmail and Outlook) or use a seed-list tool, and see if it lands in the inbox or spam.

faq.q: What if every inbox goes red at once?
faq.a: Stop sending and check your list and DNS records first. That usually means a list or setup problem, not one bad inbox.
